titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Ascension and the Second Coming in the Prophets (ch. 111)
part: ch. 111 — the ascension and the second coming in the prophets
about: Chapter 111 turns the author's proof from the prophets to Christ's ascension and return. David (Psalms 68, 21, 18, 24 and 62), Amos, Zechariah (14:4–5) and Daniel (7:13–14) are quoted in the usual frame 'and as X prophesied, he said', with the question 'who is this king of glory?' from Psalm 24 at the centre. The Amos quotation does not match any verse I can identify. The author then says that nothing happened without the prophets, who prophesied in deed as well as word, and gives Abraham's descent into Egypt and return in wealth as the type of Christ's descent and ascent. Two units (47 and 48 words) hold several quotations with no ፤ and stay whole. The quotations often differ from the psalms and prophets as they are usually known, so notes name a source only where clear and flag doubtful words with (?). Dillmann's lexicon was not available for this draft.

sentences.i: Chapter 111: Concerning his ascension and his second coming
sentences.n: Chapter heading: 'Concerning his ascension and his second coming'. ፻፲፩ is the numeral 111 (፻ hundred, ፲ ten, ፩ one). በእንተ 'concerning' takes ዕርገቱ: ዕርገት 'ascension' (from ዐረገ 'go up') + -ሁ 'his' (written ዕርገቱ). ወዳግም ምጽአቱ is ወ- 'and' + ዳግም 'second' + ምጽአቱ: ምጽአት 'coming' (from መጽአ 'come') + -ሁ 'his'; ዳግም qualifies ምጽአቱ, so 'and his second coming'. The chapter is another catena of prophecies, each opened by ወበከመ ተነበየ X ወይቤ 'and as X prophesied, he said', as in the previous part.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ወአበው ፡ ቀደምት ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዕርገቱ ፡ ወዳግም ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ይኰንን ፡ ሕያዋነ ፡ ወሙታነ ፡ ወዳዊትኒ ፡ ይቤ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዕርገቱ ፡ ዐረገ ፡ ውስተ ፡ አርያም ፡ ፄዊወከ ፡ ፄዋ ፡ ወወህብከ ፡ ጸጋከ ፡ ለእጓለ ፡ እመሕያው ፤
sentences.l: And-as they-prophesied prophets all and-fathers ancient much concerning ascension-his and-second coming-his, he-will-judge living and-dead; and-David-too said concerning ascension-his: 'He-ascended into height; you-took-captive(?) captivity(?), and-you-gave grace-your to-child-of mankind;
sentences.i: As all the prophets and the fathers of old prophesied at length(?) about his ascension and his second coming — that he will judge the living and the dead — so David also said about his ascension: 'He went up into the height; you took a captivity captive(?), and gave your grace to mankind;
sentences.n: Psalm 68:18 (67:19 in the Greek numbering), applied to the ascension (Ephesians 4:8 applies it so too). The frame is double: ወበከመ ተነበዩ 'and as they prophesied' (tä-stem perfect of ነበየ, 3mp) opens a comparison, and ወዳዊትኒ ይቤ 'and David too said' (ዳዊት + emphatic -ኒ) completes it. ነቢያት ኵሎሙ 'all the prophets' (ኵሎሙ is ኵሉ + -ሙ, 'all of them'); አበው ቀደምት 'the fathers of old'; ብዙኀ, accusative 'much', which I take as an adverb, 'at length' (?). ይኰንን is the 3ms imperfect of ኰነነ 'judge': 'he will judge', or 'who will judge'; ሕያዋነ ወሙታነ 'living and dead' are plural accusatives. In the quotation: ዐረገ 'he went up'; አርያም 'the height, high heaven'. ፄዊወከ ፄዋ looks like a figura etymologica, 'you took captive a captivity', with ፄዋ 'captivity'; but ፄዊወከ is not the 2ms perfect I would expect (ፄወውከ), so I take its sense from the pairing with ፄዋ, and the root ፄወወ 'take captive' is unconfirmed without Dillmann (?). ወወህብከ is ወ- 'and' + ወሀብከ 'you gave' (2ms perfect; this ወ is a root letter); ጸጋ 'grace, gift' + -ከ 'your'. ለእጓለ እመሕያው is ለ- 'to' + እጓለ 'child of' + እመሕያው 'mankind', the usual Geʿez 'to mankind'. The unit ends at ፤ with the quotation still open.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ወፂእየ ፡ እገብእ ፡ ወእትመየጥ ፡ እንተ ፡ ቀላየ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-again said God: 'Having-gone-out I-will-return, and-I-will-turn-back, which(?) depths-of(?) sea;
sentences.i: And again God said: 'Having gone out, I will return and turn back(?) from(?) the depths of the sea;
sentences.n: Psalm 68:22 (67:23 in the Greek numbering): in the psalm God brings his people back out of the sea, but the Geʿez has the speaker himself returning. ወፂእየ is the converb (gerund) of ወጽአ 'go out' with the 1cs ending -የ, 'having gone out'; its first ወ is a root letter, not 'and'. እገብእ 'I will return' (ገብአ); ወእትመየጥ 'and I will turn back' (ወ- + 1cs imperfect, tä-stem of መይጠ 'turn'). እንተ is the feminine relative pronoun 'which', which fits poorly before ቀላየ ባሕር; I take it as standing for 'from' (?), and ቀላየ as the construct state of ቀላይ, 'depths of' (?), a guess from the psalm's sense, not from a known entry. ባሕር 'sea'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዘምሩ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘዐርገ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰማይ ፤
sentences.l: And-again said: 'Sing to-God, who-ascended into heaven;
sentences.i: And again he said: 'Sing to God, who went up into heaven;
sentences.n: Psalm 68:32–33 (67:33–34 in the Greek numbering). ዘምሩ is the imperative plural of ዘመረ 'sing, praise with song'; ለእግዚኣብሔር 'to God'; ዘዐርገ 'who ascended' (relative ዘ- + perfect). ሰማይ 'heaven'. The quotation runs on into the next unit.

sentences.i: the heaven that lies toward the east.'
sentences.n: Psalm 68:33 (67:34 in the Greek numbering). ሰማይ repeats the ሰማይ of the previous unit in apposition and adds ዘመንገለ ጽባሕ: ዘ- 'which (is)' + መንገለ 'toward' + ጽባሕ 'east, morning', 'the heaven that is toward the east'. The psalm has more at this point (a 'heaven of heavens'); here only 'heaven' remains. The ascension is thus set toward the east, which may be why Zechariah's Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, follows (?). The source prints this short unit as a separate sentence and I keep it so.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ አሞጽ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ መሲሕ ፡ ዘይገብር ፡ ጊዜ ፡ በጽሐ ፡ ወይትሌዐል ፡ እምድር ፡ ውስተ ፡ አርያም ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Amos prophet and-said: 'Messiah, who-does(?): time has-arrived(?), and-he-will-be-exalted from-earth to height;
sentences.i: And as the prophet Amos prophesied, he said: 'The Messiah, who acts(?): the time has come(?), and he will be exalted from the earth to the height;
sentences.n: I cannot match these words to a verse of Amos; Amos 9:6 and 4:13 (the Lord in the heights, and the formula of his name) are the nearest, so this may be a paraphrase (?). መሲሕ 'Messiah'. The clause ዘይገብር ጊዜ በጽሐ is hard: ዘይገብር 'who does, who makes' (ዘ- + 3ms imperfect of ገብረ), then ጊዜ በጽሐ 'the time has arrived' (ጊዜ 'time', በጽሐ 3ms perfect). The two parts are loosely joined; perhaps 'who acts when the time has come' (?), and I keep it uncertain. ይትሌዐል 'he will be exalted' (3ms imperfect/jussive of ተለዐለ, tä-stem of the root l-ʿ-l 'be high'); እምድር is እም- 'from' + ምድር 'earth'; ውስተ አርያም 'into the height'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ስሙ ፡ ዘኵሎ ፡ ይመልክ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ተለዐልከ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ በኀይልከ ፡ ንሴብሕ ፡ ወንዜምር ፡ ለጽንዕከ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዘካርያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወይቀውማ ፡ እገሪሁ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ደብረ ፡ ዘይት ፡ ጽባሒሃ ፡ ለኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ወተጽዕነ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ኪሩቤል ፡ ወሰረረ ፡ በክነፈ ፡ ነፋስ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አርኅዉ ፡ ኆኃተ ፡ መኳንንት ፡ ወይትረኀዋ ፡ ኆኃት ፡ እለ ፡ እምፍጥረት ፡ ወይባእ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ፤
sentences.l: And-God name-his, who-all he-rules.' And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'You-were-exalted, O-Lord, in-your-might; we-praise and-we-sing to-your-strength.' And-as prophesied Zechariah prophet and-said: 'And-will-stand feet-his upon mountain-of olive, her-east, of-Jerusalem; and-he-was-borne(?) upon cherubim, and-sped(?) on-wing-of wind.' And-as said David: 'Open gates-of nobles, and-let-be-opened gates which from-creation, and-let-enter king-of glory;
sentences.i: And God is his name, who rules over all.' And as the prophet David prophesied, he said: 'You were exalted, Lord, in your might; we will praise and sing to your strength.' And as the prophet Zechariah prophesied, he said: 'His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem; and he rode(?) on the cherubim, and sped(?) on the wing of the wind.' And as David said: 'Open the gates of the nobles, and let the gates that are from creation be opened, and let the king of glory enter;
sentences.n: Five quotations run together in the longest unit of the part (47 words, no ፤ inside, so it stays whole). (1) ወእግዚኣብሔር ስሙ ዘኵሎ ይመልክ finishes the Amos saying of the previous unit, 'and God is his name, who rules all': ዘ- 'who' + ኵሎ 'all' (accusative, object) + ይመልክ (3ms imperfect of መልከ 'rule'); Amos 4:13 and 9:6 contain a similar formula, so the closing quotation mark is placed here. (2) Psalm 21:13 (20:13 in the Greek numbering): ተለዐልከ 'you were exalted' (2ms perfect), በኀይልከ 'in your might', ንሴብሕ ወንዜምር 'we will praise and sing' (1cp), ለጽንዕከ 'to your strength'. (3) Zechariah 14:4: ወይቀውማ 'and will stand' (read as 3fp imperfect, agreeing with እገሪሁ 'his feet' (?)), ደብረ ዘይት 'the Mount of Olives' (ደብር 'mountain' in construct, ዘይት 'olive'), ጽባሒሃ ለኢየሩሳሌም 'her east, Jerusalem's' (ጽባሒ 'east' + -ሃ 'her', then ለ- names the possessor), so 'east of Jerusalem'. (4) Without a new frame, Psalm 18:10 (17:11): ወተጽዕነ ላዕለ ኪሩቤል 'and he was borne upon cherubim', so 'rode' (ተጽዕነ, passive of ጸዐነ 'load', stem unconfirmed (?)); ወሰረረ 'and he sped' is uncertain (?); በክነፈ ነፋስ 'on the wing of the wind' (ክነፍ construct before ነፋስ). (5) Psalm 24:7–9 (23:7–9): አርኅዉ 'open!' (imperative pl.), ኆኃተ መኳንንት 'the gates of the nobles' (the psalm itself calls on the gates to lift up their heads; why nobles here I cannot say (?)), ወይትረኀዋ 'and let them be opened' (jussive, fem. pl.), ኆኃት እለ እምፍጥረት 'the gates that are from creation' (እለ plural relative, እም- 'from', ፍጥረት 'creation'), ወይባእ 'and let him enter' (jussive of ቦአ), ንጉሠ ስብሐት 'the king of glory' (ንጉሥ in construct state before ስብሐት 'glory'). The English marks only the quotations the grammar shows; the last is left open because the source never closes it.

sentences.t: መኑ ፡ ውእ ፡ ቱ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ፤
sentences.i: Who is he, this king of glory?
sentences.n: Psalm 24:8 (23:8). The source prints ውእ ፡ ቱ with a wordspace inside the word, 'ውእ ቱ'; this is a printing oddity, and the word is ውእቱ 'he, it is' (3ms pronoun), kept as printed in the Geʿez. መኑ 'who?'; ዝንቱ 'this' (masculine); ንጉሠ ስብሐት is the construct state, 'king of glory' (ንጉሠ, the construct state of ንጉሥ 'king', before ስብሐት 'glory'). The unit ends at ፤ because the answer follows.

sentences.t: እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኀያል ፡ ወጽኑዕ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ኀያል ፡ በውስተ ፡ ፀብእ ፤
sentences.l: The-Lord strong and-firm, the-Lord strong in-the-midst-of battle;
sentences.i: The Lord, strong and firm; the Lord, strong in the midst of battle;
sentences.n: Psalm 24:8 (23:8), the first answer to the question. ኀያል 'strong, mighty' and ወጽኑዕ 'and firm' (ወ- + ጽኑዕ 'firm, strong'). The answer is built as a pair: እግዚኣብሔር ኀያል ወጽኑዕ 'the Lord, strong and firm', then እግዚአብሔር ኀያል 'the Lord, strong' again, now with በውስተ ፀብእ: በ- 'in' + ውስተ 'into, in the midst of' + ፀብእ 'battle, war'. Note the two spellings of 'God' in this chapter, እግዚአብሔር and እግዚኣብሔር, both 'the Lord God'; I do not mark them as different.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ አጠየቀ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ አርኅዉ ፡ ኆኃተ ፡ መኳንንት ፡ ወይትረኀዋ ፡ ኆኃት ፡ እለ ፡ እምፍጥረት ፡ ወይባእ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-asked(?) and-said: 'Open gates-of nobles, and-let-be-opened gates which from-creation, and-let-enter king-of glory;
sentences.i: And again he asked(?), and said: 'Open the gates of the nobles, and let the gates that are from creation be opened, and let the king of glory enter;
sentences.n: Psalm 24:9 (23:9), the second call, in the same words as the quotation in the long unit above (see its notes: አርኅዉ imperative pl.; ወይትረኀዋ and ወይባእ jussives). ወካዕበ 'and again'; አጠየቀ is uncertain: it looks like the causative a-stem of ጠየቀ 'be exact', here perhaps 'he pressed, asked closely' (?), which suits the question that follows.

sentences.i: Who is he, this king of glory?
sentences.n: Psalm 24:10 (23:10), repeated. Here ውእቱ is printed whole, unlike the earlier ውእ ቱ.

sentences.t: እግዚአብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ ኀያላን ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ስብሐት ።
sentences.l: The-Lord God-of the-mighty is-he, this king-of glory.'
sentences.i: The Lord, the God of the mighty, he is this king of glory.'
sentences.n: Psalm 24:10 (23:10). The psalm's usual 'Lord of hosts' is here አምላከ ኀያላን 'God of the mighty (ones)' (አምላክ construct before ኀያላን, plural of ኀያል). ውእቱ is the pronoun 'he' serving as copula ('is'), followed by ዝንቱ 'this': 'he is this king of glory'. The ። closes the long run of quotations on the ascension.

sentences.t: ወበእንተ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ዳግመ ፡ ይኴንን ፡ ሕያዋነ ፡ ወሙታነ ፡ ዘሎቱ ፡ ስብሐት ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፤
sentences.l: And-concerning coming-his again he-will-judge living and-dead, to-whom glory for-age-of age, Amen;
sentences.i: And concerning his coming again, that he will judge the living and the dead, to whom be glory for ever and ever, Amen;
sentences.n: The author turns from the ascension to the return. ወበእንተ 'and concerning' (ወ- + በእንተ); ዳግመ is the accusative of ዳግም 'again'; ይኴንን 'he will judge' is the verb of unit 1 (ይኰንን, from ኰነነ): the two spellings differ in the vowel after the labiovelar (ኰ first order, ኴ fifth), and I leave both as printed without explaining the difference (?). ዘሎቱ ስብሐት 'to whom (is) glory' (ዘ- 'who' + ሎቱ 'to him'). ለዓለመ ዓለም 'for ever and ever', literally 'to the age of the age' (the construct ዓለመ), an ending that recurs; አሜን 'amen'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዘካርያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ውእተ ፡ አሚረ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላኪየ ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ ቅዱሳኒሁ ፡ ምስሌሁ ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Zechariah prophet: 'In-that day he-will-come the-Lord my-God, and-all-of-them his-saints with-him.'
sentences.i: And as the prophet Zechariah prophesied: 'On that day the Lord my God will come, and all of them, his saints, with him.'
sentences.n: Zechariah 14:5, with the order of the last clause as the Geʿez has it. ውእተ አሚረ 'on that day' (a fixed accusative phrase of time: ውእተ 'that' and አሚር 'day'). ይመጽእ 'he will come' (3ms imperfect of መጽአ). አምላኪየ 'my God' (አምላክ + 1cs -የ, with a linking vowel -ኢ-); ወኵሎሙ 'and all of them'; ቅዱሳኒሁ 'his saints' (ቅዱስ, plural ቅዱሳን, + -ሁ); ምስሌሁ 'with him' (ምስለ with the suffix -ሁ, stem ምስሌ-).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ምዕረ ፡ ነበበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወዘንተ ፡ ክመ ፡ ሰማዕኩ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'Once spoke God, and-this too(?) I-heard;
sentences.i: And as the prophet David prophesied, he said: 'Once God spoke, and this too(?) I heard;
sentences.n: Psalm 62:11 (61:12 in the Greek numbering): the psalm has God speaking once and the psalmist hearing two things. ምዕረ 'once'; ነበበ 'he spoke' (3ms perfect of ነበበ, not the verb of ተነበየ 'prophesied'); ወዘንተ is ወ- + ዘንተ, 'and this' (accusative of ዝንቱ). ክመ is not a form I know: I read it as 'also, too' (?), but it may be a corruption of ከመ 'thus' (?) or stand for 'two', as in the psalm (?). ሰማዕኩ 'I heard' (1cs perfect). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ዘእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ሣህል ፡ ወዚአከ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ኀይል ፡ እስመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ትፈድዮ ፡ ለኵሉ ፡ በከመ ፡ ምግባሩ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳንኤል ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ርኢኩ ፡ በራእየ ፡ ሌሊት ፡ ወናሁ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወልደ ፡ እጓለ ፡ እመሕያው ፡ ኀበ ፡ ብሉየ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ ወተውህበ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ምኵናን ፡ ወክብር ፡ ወመንግሥት ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ አሕዛብ ፡ ወነገድ ፡ ወበሓውርት ፡ ተቀንዩ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወምኵናኑኒ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ማኅለቅተ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፨
sentences.l: for of-the-Lord mercy, and-yours, O-Lord, might; for you you-repay-him(?) to-all according-as deed-his.' And-as prophesied Daniel prophet and-said: 'I-saw in-vision-of night, and-behold he-came like son-of child-of mankind to the-aged-of days; and-was-given to-him authority and-honour and-kingdom, and-all peoples and-tribe and-in-goings(?) served to-him; and-authority-his-too, which has-not end, until for-age-of age, Amen.'
sentences.i: for mercy is the Lord's, and yours, Lord, is might; for you repay everyone according to his deed.' And as the prophet Daniel prophesied, he said: 'I saw in a vision of the night, and behold, he came like a son of the offspring of man to the old one of days; and authority and honour and kingdom were given to him, and all peoples and tribes, and in journeys(?), served him; and his authority too, which has no end, on to ever and ever, Amen.'
sentences.n: Two quotations in one 48-word unit with no ፤ inside, so it stays whole: the end of Psalm 62:12 (61:13), then Daniel 7:13–14. እስመ 'for'; ዘእግዚኣብሔር ሣህል 'of the Lord (is) mercy' (ዘ- 'of' marks the possessor, put first); ወዚአከ 'and yours' (ዚአ- + -ከ); ትፈድዮ 'you repay' (2ms imperfect of ፈደየ 'repay, requite'; the final -ዮ is perhaps a 3ms object suffix anticipating ለኵሉ (?)), ለኵሉ 'to all', በከመ ምግባሩ 'according to his deed' (ምግባር + -ሁ). Daniel: ርኢኩ 'I saw'; ራእይ 'vision'; ወናሁ 'and behold'; ከመ ወልደ እጓለ እመሕያው 'like a son of the offspring of man' (ወልደ in its construct/accusative form; the Geʿez doubles the 'son of man' phrase, which English renders 'son of man'); ብሉየ መዋዕል 'the old one of days', the title English calls the 'Ancient of Days'; ተውህበ ሎቱ 'was given to him'; ምኵናን 'authority' (also 'judgment'), ክብር 'honour', መንግሥት 'kingdom'. ነገድ 'tribe'. ወበሓውርት is uncertain: ሓውርት (from ሖረ 'go') would be 'goings, journeys', but one expects 'languages' at this point in Daniel, so the word, or the whole phrase, may be corrupt (?). ተቀንዩ 'they served' (3mp perfect, tä-stem of ቀነየ 'serve, be subject' (?)). ወምኵናኑኒ 'and his authority too', ዘአልቦ ማኅለቅተ 'which has no end' (ማኅለቅት 'end' in the accusative after አልቦ). እስከ ለዓለመ ዓለም 'until for ever and ever'. The ፨ closes the quotations and turns to the author's own argument.

sentences.t: ወኵሎሙ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ትንቢተ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ነገሩ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ ወዘይከውን ፡ ዘተገብረ ፡ ወዘይትገበር ፡ ዘቀዳሚ ፡ ወዘደኃሪ ፡ ወእስከ ፡ ዳግም ፡ ምጽአቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-all prophets prophesied, and-there-is-not what happened without prophecy-of prophets; and-all matters-his, what happened and-what will-be, what was-done and-what is-done, what-first and-what-last, and until second coming-his;
sentences.i: All the prophets prophesied, and nothing has happened without the prophecy of the prophets; and all his matters, what has happened and what will be, what was done and what is done, what is first and what is last, and up to his second coming;
sentences.n: The author's comment on the whole catena: nothing has happened without the prophets. ወአልቦ ዘኮነ ዘእንበለ ትንቢተ ነቢያት 'there is nothing that happened without the prophecy of the prophets': አልቦ 'there is not', ዘኮነ 'that was, happened' (ዘ- + perfect of ኮነ), ዘእንበለ 'without', ትንቢተ the construct of ትንቢት 'prophecy'. Then three pairs, each joined by ወዘ-: ዘኮነ ወዘይከውን 'what has been and what will be' (perfect and imperfect of ኮነ), ዘተገብረ ወዘይትገበር 'what was done and what is done' (perfect and imperfect of the passive tä-stem of ገብረ), ዘቀዳሚ ወዘደኃሪ 'what is first and what is last' (ዘ- + ቀዳሚ 'first', ደኃሪ 'last'), together 'from beginning to end'. ወእስከ ዳግም ምጽአቱ 'and until his second coming' (እስከ 'until'). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወአኮ ፡ በቃል ፡ ባሕቲቱ ፡ ዘተነበዩ ፡ ወዘተናገሩ ፡ አላ ፡ በሥጋሆሙኒ ፡ አርአዩ ፡ ዘምስለ ፡ ትንቢት ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ኮናአን ፡ ወወረደ ፡ አቡነ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ግብጸ ፡ ወገብአ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ ብዕል ፡ ወክብር ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ጥልቀት ፤
sentences.l: And-not by-word alone, what they-prophesied and-what they-spoke, but in-bodies-their-too they-showed what with prophecy; and-was famine land-of Canaan, and-went-down our-father Abraham Egypt-ward, and-returned with much wealth and-honour, without defect(?);
sentences.i: And it was not by word alone that they prophesied and spoke, but they showed in their own bodies too what goes with prophecy: there was a famine in the land of Canaan, and our father Abraham went down into Egypt, and came back with much wealth and honour, without defect(?);
sentences.n: The prophets are now said to have prophesied in deed as well as word, and the author's example is Abraham in Genesis 12:10–13:2 (famine, the descent into Egypt, the return rich). ወአኮ is ወ- + አኮ 'and not' (negating the phrase that follows); በቃል ባሕቲቱ 'by word alone' (ባሕቲቱ 'alone', ባሕቲት + -ሁ); ዘተነበዩ ወዘተናገሩ 'what they prophesied and what they spoke' (ተናገረ 'speak'), with ዘ- giving a relative sense; አላ 'but'; በሥጋሆሙኒ 'in their bodies too' (ሥጋ 'flesh' + -ሆሙ 'their' + -ኒ); አርአዩ 'they showed' (3mp perfect, causative of ርእየ); ዘምስለ ትንቢት 'what is with prophecy', or 'what accompanies prophecy'. ኮነ ረኃብ 'there was a famine' (ኮነ 'was', ረኃብ 'hunger'); ምድረ ኮናአን 'the land of Canaan' (ምድር construct, ኮናአን Canaan). ወረደ 'went down'; አቡነ አብርሃም 'our father Abraham'; ግብጸ 'Egypt', accusative (ግብጽ), so 'went down to Egypt'. ገብአ 'returned'; ምስለ ብዙኅ ብዕል ወክብር 'with much wealth and honour'. ዘእንበለ ጥልቀት 'without' + ጥልቀት: an earlier part glossed ጥልቀት 'defect, depth (?)'; I keep 'defect' (?), and Dillmann was not available. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወከማሁ ፡ ወረደ ፡ መድኀኒነ ፡ ወአድኀነ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ክርስቲያኑ ፡ ማኅበረ ፡ አሕዛብ ፡ ወዐርገ ፡ ነሢኦ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወስብሐተ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-likewise went-down our-saviour and-saved house-of his-Christians, assembly-of nations; and-ascended, having-taken glory and-praise. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And likewise our Saviour went down and saved his church, the assembly of the nations; and he ascended, having taken glory and praise.
sentences.n: The type is drawn: as Abraham went down to Egypt and came back in wealth, so Christ went down and rose in glory. ወከማሁ 'and likewise' (ከማሁ 'thus, so'); ወረደ 'went down'; መድኀኒነ 'our saviour' (መድኀኒ + -ነ); ወአድኀነ 'and saved' (causative of ድኅነ, 'be saved'); ቤተ ክርስቲያኑ 'his church', literally 'the house of his Christians' (ቤተ construct, ክርስቲያን + -ሁ), glossed by ማኅበረ አሕዛብ 'the assembly of nations' (ማኅበር construct, 'gathering'); ወዐርገ 'and he ascended'; ነሢኦ is the converb of ነሥአ 'take', 'having taken'; ክብረ ወስብሐተ 'glory and praise' (accusatives). The unit ends with ፨, and the run of six ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is kept attached to it as printed, presumably marking the end of the chapter and of the section on the prophets of the ascension.
